notes: Responses on the v2 HTTP and WebSocket APIs are now faster to build and smaller on the wire.
The order of the JSON keys inside `structuredContent` has changed on those two APIs. Every field, value, and type is the same. Read fields by name, not by position.
Whole numbers larger than 2^53 in `structuredContent` are now exact. They were previously rounded.
Ticks now resolve faster when several members of the same faction act in the same tick. Faction achievement progress is calculated once per faction per tick instead of once per action.
Distress calls no longer push missions into your queue. A mayday now posts a single rescue mission that anyone who heard it can claim, so your mission list only holds jobs you chose.
To answer a mayday, call `accept_mission` with the `mission_id` from the emergency broadcast. You do not need to be docked, and the first pilot to claim it gets it.

A claimed rescue counts toward your 5-mission limit like any other mission. Rescues that were auto-assigned to you before this release are cleared, so they no longer block you from accepting new work.
`distress_signal` now returns `mission_id` and `responders_reached` (how many pilots heard you) in place of `missions_sent`.

Fewer dead-end distress calls: pirate bait now only comes from raiders actually sitting in their ambush, server-generated calls expire after 30 minutes instead of 3 hours, and a call is no longer broadcast when no wreck will be there.
If you claim a rescue for the system you are already in, travelling to any point of interest now completes it. Previously you had to jump out and back.
Muting the `chat.emergency` notification channel now genuinely opts you out of distress calls entirely.

Fixed a stall that slowed one tick every five minutes. Faction achievement progress was recalculated once per faction member instead of once per faction, so large factions made the whole server lag. Actions submitted during those ticks now resolve on time.
New players and respawning players now get their ship's full starting loadout, not just a mining laser.
Crimson and Outer Rim starter ships now launch with energy weapons instead of autocannons -- no ammo to buy or load for your starting weapon.
Dying repeatedly at the same base can now put you back into a starter ship you already have there, instead of always giving you a brand-new one.

Exchange mission text now states the real completion rule: your order counts only once a counterparty fills it, not when you place it. The wording also clarifies that credits held in escrow for a buy order are not cargo.
A mission you already accepted keeps the text it was issued with until you take it again. The objective itself behaved this way all along.

Breaking change for scripts: on `facility` `action=faction_owned`, the fields `total_rent_per_cycle`, `arrears_owed` and `note` have moved into a `faction_rent` object. Read them at `faction_rent.total_rent_per_cycle` and so on. Nothing was removed, only relocated.
That `faction_rent` object also reports the facility count, an estimated rent per day, and the eviction grace window, so you can see how many missed cycles you have before a facility is repossessed.
`facility` `action=faction_list` now reports the same `faction_rent` summary, so you no longer need a second call to see what the faction owes.

The refining and crafting skill descriptions now state what those skills actually do. The refining efficiency and bulk crafting bonuses they advertised were never active, and the catalog no longer lists them.
The `ip_timed_out` websocket error now carries `details.retry_after`, `details.limit` and `details.scope`, so you can wait exactly as long as the block lasts instead of guessing a backoff.
Renouncing your last citizenship now sticks across a server restart. You stay stateless until you take a new citizenship, and your tax treatment follows that stateless status.

Survey mission stops now count in any order. Arriving at the last-listed system first used to do nothing — "Local Sector Survey", "Deep Space Cartography" and "Beyond the Edge" no longer make you fly back to a system you already charted.

Mission progress now comes back in the response of the command that caused it. `jump`, `dock`, `mine`, `buy`, `sell`, `create_buy_order`, `create_sell_order`, `sell_wreck`, `scrap_wreck` and `survey_system` return a `missions` section when an objective advances, so you no longer have to call `get_active_missions` to notice. The section is sent only when something changed — absent still means unchanged.
`dock` now also returns a `cargo` section, so mission cargo handed to you on arrival shows up immediately instead of leaving a stale hold.
If you are already parked in a survey mission's final system, you still need to jump out and back for the stop to register. There is no sweep of where you are already sitting.
Kill and crafting objectives still resolve between commands, so keep using `get_active_missions` for those.
Fixed sovereign mints failing to buy affordable missing inputs when complementary supplies are already in station storage.
Sovereign-mint shortages now report `buy_order_available` and direct deliveries only to inputs with active public station buy orders.
Faction action logs now record fuel withdrawals by members and allies, including the pilot, station, and fuel amount.
Filter get_action_log by your faction_id and event_type="faction.refuel" to inspect your faction's fuel withdrawals.
Receive one combined personal weekly tax statement with calculation details and machine-readable data. Retrieve the latest statement with get_tax_estimate.
Find missed-tax balances and pay_bounty guidance directly in your tax estimate. Pay an empire's full bounty remotely; prepay_tax reserves money for future assessments.

Fully inactive characters skip weekly personal taxes after a full tracked period. Gameplay and economic activity count even without a fresh login. Existing debt remains due; skipped taxes never become catch-up bills.
Tax countdowns now follow remaining game ticks and the current tick duration.
Improve loading efficiency for the default public battle history.
Mission deliveries now check the full required quantity before consuming cargo or stored goods.
Pickup missions can be retried after freeing cargo space, and crafting requirements count the same inventory shown in mission progress.
Recovery jobs now retire when their wreck disappears and pay successful recoveries from their reserved funding.
Mission expiry and progress survive persistence more consistently, including server restarts.
Community contributions and faction mission parameters are reported more accurately to clients.

An armed faction station now joins any battle in its own system where one of its members is fighting, and brings its guns to that member's side. An unarmed outpost stays out, and so does a wrecked station.

Faction stations stay out of wildlife hunts unless the creature is a leviathan. A station already in a hunt gives priority to a shared battle, including a siege. Another wildlife hunt cannot take its battle slot.

A station in a battle shuts its blast doors and refuses docking with `station_under_attack`. Because a station now joins its members' fights, plan on hitting this whenever a faction-mate fights in that system.
Medical module descriptions now name `treat_personnel(provider="field")` and distinguish active personnel treatment from automatic fleet triage.
Shipboard Sickbay describes allied treatment when the hull grants remote medical treatment capability. Field and fleet hospitals describe their own allied treatment capability.
A faction-mate of the prize claimant can now refuel and repair a stalled claimed prize with `service_prize`.
The faction must run an operational Prize Recovery Yard at any station first. A yard under construction or damaged does not unlock it.
Stop, resume, and redirect on a claimed prize remain claimant-only.
The v2 `location` state now includes `primary_color` and `secondary_color` on each entry in `nearby_players`, matching the fields `get_nearby` already returns.
`nearby_pirates` entries now carry `primary_color` and `secondary_color` when the pirate's stronghold crew has configured a livery.
Both fields are omitted when no color is set, so existing parsers need no change.
Cloaked players remain hidden from `nearby_players` as before.
